turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Howzit doc. Shame, sorry we're late, the robot on Main Road was out and this bakkie just sat there.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ag, no stress. Umm, give me a sec, the screen's frozen. Right. Sipho?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, Sipho, he's 6. School wants a note, his eyes are a proper mess after the cold.
[SEG0004] person_4 (PATIENT): My eye is all sticky and red and gross. And I can't hear myself think in that class, the boys shout and shout.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? I clicked the wrong file.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The Grade R teacher won't have him back without a note. The left eye went sticky first, then both.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which eye was first? Once more, hey.
[SEG0008] person_1 (CAREGIVER): The left one. Thursday morning it was crusted shut. Friday the right one was sticky as well.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I was gonna say Friday, but ja, she's right, Thursday morning. So four days.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Any pain in the eyes?
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): No. It doesn't hurt. Just yucky. I feel like a wet rag though.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been a bit washed out since the cold. And no, the eyes aren't sore, he keeps telling me.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is the cold itself finished?
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The runny nose stopped. And the cough's gone.
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): There's a frog in my throat still. Ribbit. I had a lekker sarmie in the car.
[SEG0016] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Ja the voice is a bit husky. Eating fine. In the waiting room he said my feet feel dead, but he was sitting on them.
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): Oh ja they're fine. I was sitting on my takkies. I've overdone it on the lego, the spaceship fell over.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. Uh, password again. Any fever with this?
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No fever. I checked this morning, normal, no temperature.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Light bothering him? Is he bumping into things, vision-wise?
[SEG0021] person_1 (CAREGIVER): No, he watches his cartoons fine. No squinting at the light.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He read the poster in the passage just now.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tummy, chest, waterworks, anything else?
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, all of that's fine. Just the eyes and being a bit tired.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines, anything?
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing. No allergies.
[SEG0027] person_1 (CAREGIVER): He still has the eczema on the elbows. That's old, not from this.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, eczema, ongoing, it's on the file. Not today's problem I don't think.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His dad gets terrible hayfever in spring. Sipho doesn't, not really.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): What have you put in the eyes?
[SEG0031] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Saline drops from Clicks. One drop, 3 times a day, since Friday. And a warm facecloth.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I nearly gave him my piraton last night. Then I thought no, that's mine, so I didn't.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Sorry, the drops again? One drop, 3 times, saline?
[SEG0034] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Ja. One drop, three times a day.
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): The drops are cold! And Biscuit ate my crayon. He's our dog.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Both eyes are red on the white part, yellow crust on the lashes, corneas are clear, lids aren't swollen.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They did an eye swab last winter at the clinic. I can't remember the month. They said it was borderline, not a proper infection.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Say that again? The swab?
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Eye swab, last winter sometime. Result was borderline. I haven't got the paper.

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok I won't treat that old borderline thing as a real number. Thinking aloud, sticky red eyes after a cold, could be viral conjunctivitis, could be a mild bacterial one, allergy's less likely seeing it's after the cold and he doesn't really get dad's hayfever. I'm not going to conclude it's bacterial. My leaning is viral conjunctivitis.
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no antibiotic then?

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): No antibiotic. Hygiene. Warm water, wipe from the nose side outward, his own facecloth, wash hands, don't share the towel. Carry on with the saline, one drop three times a day.
[SEG0043] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Must he stay home?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll write the school a note, most likely viral, he can go back once the gunk is less, as long as you're wiping. I'll do it before you leave.
[SEG0045] person_4 (PATIENT): Can I go if I don't touch my eye? I want to show the spaceship. Well. The broken one.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you don't rub, ja. Mom and aunty do the wiping.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if it doesn't come right?
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back if it's not settling in five days, or sooner if the eye gets sore, the light starts to hurt, or the lids swell.
[SEG0049] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Five days, or sooner if it's sore or swollen. Sharp.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, inbox popped up. Yes. Five days, or sooner for pain, light hurting, or swollen lids. And no antibiotic drops from the chemist, hey.
[SEG0051] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ok we won't. Thanks doc.
[SEG0052] person_4 (PATIENT): Bye! Biscuit's waiting. The frog is still in my throat but the eyes are the yucky bit.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bye Sipho. Reception will print that note now-now.

spec.situation: Parent with a child with red sticky eye after a cold; school wants a note; one eye then both; no eye pain; doctor advises hygiene, no antibiotic, explains return advice.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Tiredness reported by patient, but certainty is less certain: 'feel like a wet rag though'.
Hoarse voice was reported by caregiver, not patient.
